### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/system.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 620b6e6d40c4ef11658a658e1d2c6ae3d4aeb7d6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f3b3237fe7e100d74a5816c47a058cd95f999459` — the merge of head `3a32985c1db030239bf69fa4ce972eb35b5f07c1` into base `620b6e6d40c4ef11658a658e1d2c6ae3d4aeb7d6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f3b3237fe7e100d74a5816c47a058cd95f999459 && git checkout f3b3237fe7e100d74a5816c47a058cd95f999459
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 620b6e6d40c4ef11658a658e1d2c6ae3d4aeb7d6 3a32985c1db030239bf69fa4ce972eb35b5f07c1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 620b6e6d40c4ef11658a658e1d2c6ae3d4aeb7d6 && git merge --no-ff 3a32985c1db030239bf69fa4ce972eb35b5f07c1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 620b6e6d40c4ef11658a658e1d2c6ae3d4aeb7d6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3a32985c1db030239bf69fa4ce972eb35b5f07c1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/restriction-profile.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (`FlowNodeAction`, `FLOW_BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES`, `FLOW_STRUCTURAL_NODE_TYPES`, `FlowNodeSchema.type`), packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts (`APPROVAL_NODE_TYPE`, `APPROVAL_REVISE_NODE_TYPE`), packages/spec/src/kernel/version-grammar.ts (`SEMVER_2_0_0_VERSION_PATTERN`), packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/spec/src/system/environment-artifact.zod.ts (the sibling the placement cites), packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts (the `jobs` schedule kinds the JSDoc cites), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`hooks`, `functions`, `plugins`), packages/skills/package.json (`@objectstack/skills` exists, 18.3.0), packages/spec/src/system/restriction-profile.test.ts and packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts (read as the first consumers of the shape). The remainder of the diff (changeset, the regenerated `api-surface` / `authorable-surface` / `declaration-map` / `export-origins` / `json-schema.manifest` / strictness-ledger counts / `llms.txt` and the generated `content/docs/references/**` pages) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, as a standalone PR of those files; it was read, not reviewed.

Inputs read: card #31156 body and every comment (6709115357, 6709148921, 6709173446, 6710218086 with its two open_questions); PR #31191 body, file list (16 files, +383/-11, head repo is the base repo, draft) and the net diff `origin/main...3a32985c` (merge-base `8ef4d309`); the check-runs on `3a32985c`. Judged against the tree, not the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New public exports from `@objectstack/spec/system`: `RestrictionProfileSchema` (const) and `RestrictionProfile` (type).** `src/system/index.ts` re-exports `./restriction-profile.zod` under the Provisioning and Deployment block, beside `environment-artifact.zod`; `api-surface/system.json`, `declaration-map/system.json`, `export-origins/system.json` each gain the two rows, each pointing at `src/system/restriction-profile.zod.ts`. Nothing else is re-exported (no constants, no helper), so the public surface grows by exactly those two names. **Right.** The subpath is the one the sibling envelope lives on; `kernel/` holds what describes an app, and the ruling's subject is what an environment publishes about itself.
2. **Accept set of the new shape**, read off the code: a `strictObject` with four required keys — `allowCode: boolean`, `allowScheduledAutomation: boolean`, `allowedFlowNodeTypes: FlowNodeAction[]` (the enum instance itself, not a copy; the test pins `.shape.allowedFlowNodeTypes.element` by identity), `versions: strictObject({ spec, skills })` each a string matched against `SEMVER_2_0_0_VERSION_PATTERN`. Unknown keys refused at both levels with the named surface and curated aliases. `{}` is refused with four `invalid_type` issues; `undefined` is accepted only through the holder's own `.optional()`. No default, no transform, so `z.input` equals `z.infer` (the ADR-0122 pin 841 to 842 is the correct form; `M203` was a free index on `main`). **Right**, and it matches the card's ask: the four dimensions the ruling names, the node list read from the spec's own registry and never restated, the two versions, and an absent profile meaning no restriction.
3. **The node vocabulary is `FlowNodeAction`, so `allowedFlowNodeTypes` cannot name a plugin-registered node type.** On `main`, `FlowNodeSchema.type` is an open `z.string()` (ADR-0018) and `approval` / `approval_revise` are spec-declared constants executed by `plugin-approvals`, not `FlowNodeAction` ids; the PR's own test refuses `approval`. **Right as the ruling is written** (「allowed flow node types (a closed list read from the spec's own node registry, never restated)」) — the consequence for the reader is the open question handled in ③.
4. **Generated artefacts move together.** `json-schema.manifest/system.json` gains `system/RestrictionProfile` (so cloud card 3 can consume a JSON Schema whose node enum is derived, not hand-typed); `authorable-surface/system.json` gains the four `system/RestrictionProfile:*` rows (consistent with `system/DeployBundle:*` already being there — the generator lists every strict authoring shape, so this is not a claim that an app author writes it); the strictness ledger `system/` 395 to 397 counts the two new `strictObject` sites; `llms.txt` 39 to 40 and 220 to 221 counts the new `*.zod.ts` module; the docs reference pages count 212/1635 to 213/1636. The dev reports `check:generated` with all 14 artefacts up to date and `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · docs & code guards` are green on the head. **Right.**
5. **No runtime, gate, error code or enforcement is added** — `packages/cli` untouched, nothing in `packages/spec` reads the schema. **Right**: Prime Directive 2 (no business logic in spec) and the card's split (item 2 is `packages/cli`, `domain:server`) both hold.
6. **No ADR governs this surface.** `docs/adr/**` on `main` names neither a restriction profile nor cloud#3659; the schema implements a cloud ruling quoted verbatim on the card, and the code comment cites `objectstack-ai/cloud#3659` the way `ai/agent.zod.ts` and `ai/build-progress.zod.ts` cite theirs. The ruling text ends up in no runtime string (`.describe()` / `history` carry no tracker number). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31156-restriction-profile-schema.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, with the two line-initial declarations `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, both identical to the PR body's lines. The diff publishes two new exports from a released package and nothing is removed, renamed or tightened, so `minor` is the floor the Post-Task Checklist sets for a kind other than `none` and matches what the diff publishes. `Metadata-protocol: added` holds: the spec's own authorable-surface artefact gained four rows for the shape, and the card's claim (6709173446) dispatched with `Metadata-protocol: added`. `(widening)` is one arm of the closed pair and is the right one (a new schema, nothing narrowed). The `Skills-docs: none` line gives its reason (no author-written key, no reader this release); it is prose outside this scope. The card filed `Clause-②: yes (a new spec schema)`; the PR's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the same declaration with its arm spelled. **Clause-②: yes (widening) — level and kind judged right.** No `skip-changeset` label, correctly (the diff publishes).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (6710218086):

- **Commit trailers carry `session_01FEkQ5mzXgjDYseUz8kmybe`, a one-character slip of the thread's `session_01FEkQ5nzXgjDYseUz8kmybe`, not rewritten.** Accepted. The branch is the thread's harness branch, not `claude/issue-*`, so Multi-agent discipline §3 forbids the `--force-with-lease` a rewrite needs; the trailer pair is model-free (`Co-Authored-By: Claude`, `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_…`) and the PR body footer carries the correct session URL. The slip is a provenance blemish, not a contract matter.
- **`pr_create` sent no labels.** Accepted: the order named none, the PR publishes so `skip-changeset` would be wrong, and `Auto Label` ran green.
- **Lint scoped to `packages/spec`.** Accepted: `Lint · ESLint` and the other Lint contexts on the head are green, so the repo-wide verdict is CI's and it is in.

Open question 1 — all four dimensions required (A, shipped) versus each optional with absent = unrestricted (B). **Answered: A.** The card rules one thing, that an ABSENT profile means no restriction; A keeps exactly one spelling of "no restriction" (hold no profile) and refuses `{}` and any partial profile at parse, which is Prime Directive 12 (reject off-spec input at the producer, never a lenient `??` in a consumer). B would make a forgotten key silently permissive at the one place that is meant to restrict. The only producer is cloud card 3's control plane, which knows every value. The JSDoc states the rule and the test pins both halves (`.optional()` accepts `undefined`; `{}` yields exactly four `invalid_type` issues). No change requested.

Open question 2 — a flow node whose type is outside the built-in registry (plugin-registered, including the spec-declared `approval` / `approval_revise`) cannot be named by `allowedFlowNodeTypes`; how should item 2's reader treat it? **Answered for this PR: A (ship as is); the reader rule is escalated to item 2's claim**, with this record's reading of the tree attached: `FlowNodeSchema.type` is an open string by ADR-0018, so a profile built on the closed enum necessarily leaves plugin node types unnamed; B would copy two plugin-executed ids into the closed list and C adds authorable surface with no reader. The reader rule that follows contract-first is: a node type outside `FlowNodeAction` is governed by `allowCode` (it exists only because a code plugin registered its executor), and `os validate --target` says so by name. Item 2's claim must record which rule it implements; this is not a change to this PR.

Escalations raised by this review (both for item 2 and cloud card 3, neither a change to this diff — see ④):

- `FlowNodeAction` contains `start` and `end`, which `FLOW_STRUCTURAL_NODE_TYPES` says are always legal regardless of registered executors. A profile that lists neither forbids every flow. Item 2's reader needs a stated rule (structural types always allowed, or the control plane always lists them).
- `FlowNodeAction` contains `script`, whose only job is to call a function from `defineStack({ functions })`. A profile with `allowCode: false` and `script` in `allowedFlowNodeTypes` is self-contradictory; the schema admits it. Item 2 must say which dimension wins at the `script` node (the function it names is already refused under `allowCode: false`, so the flow fails either way, but the refusal should name one rule).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/restriction-profile.zod.ts`** — judged against the ruling it implements (cloud#3659 A as quoted on the card: 「云端搭建唯一的区别是有一些限制，比如写代码是否允许，定时任务是否允许，流程允许使用到什程度」 and the card's four-dimension ask) and its first consumers (the PR's own test file, the ADR-0122 pin, the generated JSON Schema cloud card 3 will serve, and item 2's `os validate --target`).

- Every claim the JSDoc makes was read in the live tree and holds: `FlowNodeAction` at `automation/flow.zod.ts:45` with `FLOW_BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES = FlowNodeAction.options` (line 81), so "the same list" is literally true and a type the registry gains is allowable the release it lands; `SEMVER_2_0_0_VERSION_PATTERN` at `kernel/version-grammar.ts` is anchored, accepts prereleases (`18.4.0-beta.1` in the test's fixture) and refuses `v18.4.0`, `18.4`, `latest`, `18.04.0`, `^18.4.0` — the test's six refusals are exactly that pattern's documented cells; flows of `type: 'schedule'` exist (`flow.zod.ts:1162`); `jobs` with `cron` / `interval` / `once` schedules exist (`system/job.zod.ts`); `hooks`, `functions`, `plugins` are the stack's code-carrying keys (`stack.zod.ts:1194,1225,1344`); `@objectstack/skills` is a real workspace package (18.3.0), so `versions.skills` names a version that exists.
- Composition is the repo's standard one: `lazySchema` wrapping `strictObject(options, shape).describe(…)`, the exact form in `strict-object.ts`'s own example. `strictObject` records the declaration at construction, so the alias-integrity audit judges the `aliases` table: every alias key is one the shape rejects and every target (`allowCode`, `allowScheduledAutomation`, `allowedFlowNodeTypes`, `versions`; nested `spec`, `skills`) is one it accepts. The dev's full spec suite (912 files) ran green, which includes that audit, and `Spec property liveness` is green on the head. Through the `lazySchema` Proxy, `.shape`, `.optional()` and `.safeParse` all bind to the real instance, which is why the identity test on `.shape.allowedFlowNodeTypes.element` is sound rather than accidental.
- Tried to break it: (a) `allowedFlowNodeTypes: ['start', 'start']` parses — duplicates are not refused. A set spelled as an array with no uniqueness refinement; harmless to any reader (membership test), and the control plane is the only producer. Noted, no finding. (b) A profile may be internally inconsistent (`allowCode: false` + `script`; no `start`/`end`) — the schema is a shape and the ruling asks for four independent dimensions, so refusing cross-dimension contradictions here would put reader policy into spec, which Prime Directive 2 forbids; these are escalated in ③ to item 2, where the rule belongs. **Should-fix, non-blocking, optional for this PR:** one sentence in the `allowedFlowNodeTypes` docblock saying that `start` / `end` are structural and that a `script` node is also subject to `allowCode`, so the first reader does not have to rediscover it. (c) `versions` cannot express "unknown" or a range — correct: the ruling wants the versions the environment runs, and `version-grammar.ts` says a range is a different concept judged elsewhere. (d) No `.min(1)` on `allowedFlowNodeTypes` — an empty list meaning "no built-in node type" is the honest reading of a closed allow-list and is tested; a profile with everything on is spelled by listing every id, which the test also pins from `FLOW_BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES`. (e) `strictObject` on both levels means a future `versions.runtime` or `versions.cli` is a deliberate widening with a changeset, not a silent addition; that is the right default for a published contract.
- Ablation evidence in the report (node vocabulary, version grammar, closed shape, required) each turned the expected assertions red and nothing else, each leg restored to blob `fe21c2b8`, which is the blob this diff carries for the file. The tests import from `src`, so no `dist` staleness could mask a leg.
- No must-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/system/index.ts`** — judged against the entry-point discipline the sibling `environment-artifact.zod.ts` docblock states (one entry point per name, the dual-source trap) and against `export-origins/system.json`. The barrel adds one `export *` under the Provisioning and Deployment block, after `environment-artifact.zod`, with a two-line comment naming the ruling and the absent-means-unrestricted rule. `RestrictionProfile` / `RestrictionProfileSchema` collide with nothing on `main` (grep of `packages/**` finds no prior declaration; `export-origins` maps both names to the one file), and the test pins that the system entry re-exports the very same instance. No second entry declares or re-exports the name. No finding.

Check-runs on `3a32985c` at the time of this record: every completed gate-carrying context is `success` — `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped ·` (three), `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Auto Label`, `filter`, `Plan Test Core shards`; `Lint UI`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shards and the opt-in harnesses are `skipped` by their own path filters. Still `in_progress` at this reading: `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Type Check · workspace` / `debt ledger` / `consumer gates`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` (1 to 8 of 8), `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (1 to 16 of 16), `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not wait on them and they are not pre-judged here. The seat lands only once every required context reads `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`), and the PR is a draft that must be readied first. Nothing in this PR touches a governed surface, so no Tier H approval is owed; this record is the Clause-② contract review the card's claim (6709173446) owes before enqueue.
